title: Close Update: Wall Street Retreats With Dow Halting Three-Day Winning Streak
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Retreats With Dow Halting Three-Day Winning Streak January 29, 2018, 04:23:07 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Wall Street skidded lower on Monday, stemming a three-day winning streak for the Dow Jones Industrial Average as the measure posted a triple-digit decline. Losses in Apple ( AAPL ) handed the Nasdaq Composite its third retreat in four days while all of the sectors on the S&P 500 ended in the red. 
Weaker oil prices weighed on energy names, sending the group down 1.4% in the sharpest decline among the 11 S&P sectors, as the market had little fresh news to sustain the rally that has seen U.S. crude prices surge to start 2018. 
Chevron ( CVX ) and ExxonMobil ( XOM ) were among the Dow's decliners, while Caterpillar ( CAT ) posted the steepest slide, down 2.7% as industrials retreated. Apple fell 2.1% after Japan's Nikkei reported that the tech giant will cut production of its iPhone X in half for the three-month period from January, citing notifications to suppliers. 
Tech shares, the S&P's best performers over the past year, were down 0.7% on the day, with the sector in focus ahead of a big week of earnings. Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) is due Tuesday, Facebook (FB) on Wednesday and Apple and Amazon.com (AMZN) report on Thursday. 
Investors were keeping an eye on rising bond prices, with Treasuries hit overnight until gaining back some ground after data showed December's annual core personal consumption expenditures index was unchanged at 1.5% from the prior month. Personal income beat expectations but spending fell short. 
On Tuesday, the Federal Open Market Committee starts a two-day monetary policy meeting, the last with Janet Yellen as chair. While no change in the target rate is expected, investors will be parsing the statement for clues on when the next hike might be. 
Also, President Donald Trump delivers his debut State of the Union speech, with issues including immigration and trade among those to be addressed, he told reporters on Monday.
